title: Lodge a residential rental bond (landlords and agents)
summary: Landlords and property agents can lodge a residential rental bond for a tenant either through the online portal or by using a paper-based form.
intro:
If you're a self-managing landlord or property agent, you're legally required to offer a tenant the option of lodging their bond directly through Rental Bonds Online (RBO).

If the tenant is unable to access the online service, or chooses to use the paper-based method, you'll need to lodge a Rental Bond Lodgement form. This form is available through your RBO account.
what_you_need: Rental Bond Lodgement form (if using paper-based method)

how_to_steps.text: Select the 'Go to Rental Bonds Online' button and log in to your account.
Select the 'Links' section and download a Rental Bond Lodgement form.
Complete the form, and have the tenant sign it.

more_info.text: When using the paper-based method you can only take the rental bond after the tenant signs the tenancy agreement.
You cannot keep the money yourself or put it into an account in the tenant’s name.
Once a bond is received you must provide a receipt, or note the payment details on the tenancy agreement, and provide a copy to the tenant.

faqs.q: How must I lodge a bond if I am a self-managing landlord or property agent?
faqs.a: You are legally required to offer a tenant the option of lodging their bond directly through Rental Bonds Online (RBO).

faqs.q: What if the tenant cannot use the online service?
faqs.a: If the tenant is unable to access the online service, or chooses to use the paper-based method, you must lodge a Rental Bond Lodgement form.
